For personalised insurance advice on Health or Term Insurance, book a FREE call with Ditto - https://ditto.sh/4xzt16 

Unlimited sum insured (S.I.) health insurance plans provide policyholders with unparalleled flexibility, covering medical expenses without a predefined limit. These plans ensure comprehensive coverage, eliminating concerns about exhausting claim limits during expensive treatments. Popular options in this category include ICICI Lombard Elevate, ACKO Platinum Plan, and Star Superstar. These plans cater to diverse healthcare needs while offering extensive protection.

Insurance companies use actuarial science to estimate risks and liabilities associated with offering unlimited coverage. By analyzing historical claims data, they ensure financial viability while pricing these plans appropriately. Interestingly, most high-value claims are under ₹15-20 lakh, and the average claim amount paid, as per the IRDAI Annual Report 2023-24, is ₹31,086. This shows that a majority of claims fall into lower value ranges, enabling insurers to balance customer needs with sustainable pricing models.

While these plans offer peace of mind, there are potential risks and challenges. If the adoption of unlimited S.I. plans increases significantly, insurers may face higher claim frequencies, which could necessitate premium adjustments. In extreme cases, if claims consistently surpass actuarial predictions, insurers might revise their pricing models or discontinue such plans. These adjustments could lead to rapid premium hikes or limited availability of unlimited S.I. coverage in the future.

The benefits of unlimited sum insured plans are undeniable. They provide financial security by covering all medical expenses without a cap, ensuring that policyholders are never underinsured during critical illnesses or costly treatments. However, these plans come with higher premiums, and prospective buyers should evaluate their healthcare needs and financial capabilities carefully. Policyholders should also be aware of the potential for premium hikes due to increasing adoption or unforeseen claim trends.

At Ditto Insurance, we recommend a sum insured of ₹15-25 lakh for most individuals, as this range typically covers major critical illnesses. Additionally, many comprehensive plans offer renewal bonuses and unlimited restoration benefits, enhancing coverage over time. For those concerned about affordability, a minimum cover of ₹10 lakh can provide a reliable safety net for unexpected medical emergencies. However, it is crucial to choose sufficient initial coverage to avoid limitations, as increasing your sum insured later may involve new waiting periods and underwriting approvals.

Unlimited sum insured health insurance plans offer unparalleled financial protection, but their long-term sustainability depends on a balance between customer adoption, claim patterns, and pricing models. To make informed decisions, always assess your needs and explore the best plans available.

comments.author: @suyashhogade6999

comments.text:
Generally, unlimited restoration works by restoring your base sum insured once a claim is settled. In your example, after Person A’s ₹4 Lakh claim, the ₹5 Lakh base sum insured would be restored, so Person B can use it without paying from your pocket.

However, terms vary by policy — some may require waiting periods before the cover is refilled, or may not allow restoration for the same illness. It’s best to speak with one of our advisors over chat or call to understand the exact details for your policy.

comments.text:
Yes, Starting with a base sum insured of ₹25 lakh, the plan offers:

Inbuilt Cumulative Bonus: Increases the sum insured by 50% each year, up to a maximum of 100% over two years.

Cumulative Bonus Super (Optional Add-on): Provides an additional 100% increase in the sum insured each year, up to a maximum of 500% over five years.

By the end of five years, your total coverage would be:
Year 1: ₹25 lakh (base) + ₹12.5 lakh (50% inbuilt bonus) + ₹25 lakh (100% CB Super) = ₹62.5 lakh
Year 2: ₹62.5 lakh + ₹12.5 lakh (remaining 50% inbuilt bonus) + ₹25 lakh (100% CB Super) = ₹1 crore
Year 3: ₹1 crore + ₹25 lakh (100% CB Super) = ₹1.25 crore
Year 4: ₹1.25 crore + ₹25 lakh (100% CB Super) = ₹1.5 crore
Year 5: ₹1.5 crore + ₹25 lakh (100% CB Super) = ₹1.75 crore

Therefore, in the 6th year, your sum insured would be ₹1.75 crore. You can make a hospitalization claim up to this amount in a single instance, subject to the policy's terms and conditions. 

You can read more about the plan here- https://joinditto.in/health-insurance/care-insurance/care-supreme/
